title: Notice Recording Shelter Rule
subject: Real Property
stem:
A lakeside campground parcel on a county road had a small dock, six camper pads, and a locked equipment shed. On January 6, Daniel conveyed the parcel by deed to Martha as a gift. Daniel signed the deed before Abigail, a notary public, and Abigail placed her required seal on it. On February 12, after Daniel learned that Martha had not recorded her deed, Daniel purported to convey the same parcel to Philip for value. Philip did not know that Martha held any interest in the parcel. On February 20, Martha recorded her deed. In May, Philip executed a deed conveying the parcel to Abigail. Abigail immediately recorded that deed.

A statute in the jurisdiction provides: "No transfer of an interest in real property is valid against a subsequent purchaser for value without notice of the transfer unless the transfer has been recorded."
call: In litigation between Martha and Abigail, who should be declared owner of the parcel?

choices.A: Martha, because Daniel conveyed the parcel to her before any later deed.
choices.B: Abigail, because Philip bought the parcel for value before Martha recorded her deed.
choices.C: Martha, because Abigail had notice that Daniel had first conveyed the parcel to Martha.
choices.D: Philip, because he gave value for the parcel without notice of Martha's deed.

rightExplanation: Abigail owns the parcel. Philip was a subsequent purchaser for value without notice when he bought before Martha recorded. Under the notice recording statute, Philip took priority over Martha's earlier unrecorded deed. Abigail took from Philip. Under the shelter rule, a transferee from a protected bona fide purchaser receives that purchaser's priority even if the transferee herself had notice of the earlier interest. Abigail's notarization of Martha's deed therefore does not defeat the priority Abigail received through Philip.

wrongExplanations.A: First-in-time priority is attractive because Martha received the first deed. The breaker is that the notice recording statute protects Philip, who bought for value without notice before Martha recorded.
wrongExplanations.C: Abigail's notice is the strongest pull because she notarized Martha's deed. The breaker is the shelter rule: Abigail takes Philip's protected priority even though she had notice.
wrongExplanations.D: Philip's bona fide purchaser status matters and gives the answer its force. The breaker is that Philip later conveyed the parcel to Abigail, so Philip is not the owner in the litigation.
